Years ago, I changed my reason for going to the ballpark. Instead of attending simply to watch baseball, I began going to love people. The bartender noticed. Conversations deepened gradually. Nothing dramatic. No clear turning point. Just presence.

And I had to confront something in myself. I wanted results. I wanted visible fruit. I wanted clarity. Seeds, however, disappear before they grow. Growth hides underground long before it becomes visible.

In San Francisco, many are in process. Some are quietly deconstructing faith. Others are curious but cautious. God is already at work in their stories long before I arrive. My role is not to accelerate what He is maturing. It is to join Him.

I am also in process. My motives are still being purified. My desire for measurable impact still competes with simple obedience. Grace honors process because God is patient with me. So we stay present. We walk slowly with others. And we trust the Spirit to bring fruit in His time.
